canonical_question: How is the driving force for the corrosion of B2/BCC phases relative to L12/FCC phases characterized in high-entropy alloys, and is there a specific quantitative SKP voltage value provided to define this potential difference?

question_variants.question: Does the text provide specific SKP voltage values for the L12 vs B2 phases to quantify the driving force for the HEA corrosion?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text mentions that SKP maps are shown for the materials but does not provide specific numerical voltage values for the L12 vs B2 phases in the provided excerpts.

answers.answer: The document states that SKP maps are presented for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 in Figure 8b, but the specific voltage values for L12 vs B2 phases are not listed in the text provided.
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific voltage values for phases are not in the text.
evidence_spans: Here, the corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNI 2.1 EHEA in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt was investigated at 450 °C and 650 °C.
The performance of EHEA was compared with one of the benchmark dual-phase structural alloys, namely duplex steel 2205 (DS2205).
To explain the effect of eutectic microstructure on the local electrochemical activity, Scanning Kelvin Probe (SKP) analysis was utilized to measure the relative electron work function

source_evidence_spans: Respective SKP maps are shown for DS2205 in Figure 8 a and for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 in Figure 8 b

question_variants.question: Does the observed 'micro-galvanic corrosion' imply that the nobler L12/FCC phases act as cathodes specifically accelerating the dissolution of the B2/BCC phases?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text confirms that micro-galvanic corrosion occurs with the nobler L12/FCC phases compared to the B2/BCC phases, implying the nobler phases act as cathodes relative to the less noble B2/BCC phases.

answers.answer: The text states that micro-galvanic corrosion involves 'nobler L1 2 and FCC phase in EHEA and DS 2205, respectively, compared to the B2 and BCC phases', and notes 'selective dissolution of B2 phase attributed to micro-galvanic coupling', confirming the B2/BCC phases are the anodes dissolving.
answers.measurement_outcome: Selective dissolution of B2 phase observed
answers.mechanism: Micro-galvanic coupling with nobler L12/FCC phases acting as cathodes
answers.boundary_limitation: None specified for this mechanism description.
evidence_spans: Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205).
The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205.

source_evidence_spans: The phase-specific work function for the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and DS2205 suggested micro-galvanic corrosion, with nobler L1 2 and FCC phase in EHEA and DS 2205, respectively, compared to the B2 and BCC phases.

cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: One approach (PMC9955357::reader_question::99bae67618d7fa67::answer::53f5356086af6a7d) focuses on the mechanistic outcome of the potential difference, describing the 'selective dissolution' of the B2 phase in a molten salt environment. The other approach (PMC9955357::reader_question::deba89e996f1c3ef::answer::70ea02f32318a010) addresses the quantification of this potential difference, noting that while Surface Kelvin Probe (SKP) maps exist, the specific voltage values are not explicitly listed in the text.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The mechanistic confirmation of selective dissolution is observed under specific high-temperature corrosion conditions (molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt at 450 °C) [53f5356086af6a7d], whereas the lack of specific voltage values refers to SKP maps presented for the initial state at room temperature [70ea02f32318a010].
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: There are no contradictions; the answers complement each other by confirming the qualitative mechanism while identifying a specific data gap in the quantitative values within the provided text.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: The qualitative evidence for micro-galvanic coupling is strong (inferred from text description [53f5356086af6a7d]), but the quantitative evidence for the driving force magnitude is explicitly missing in the text [70ea02f32318a010].
